text:
sam: Heads up — nightly perf job shows a 8-12% p95 latency regression on 4k token generation after the dispatcher change. I attached an nsys slice and a perfetto timeline to the thread :eyes:
perf-bot: nsys profile uploaded: https://artifacts/internal/nsys/cpu_drift_1743501122.qdrep (nvtx+cuda).
kai: Did we touch kernel selection? I thought the only change was host-side serialization to remove races.
sam: Right — we removed the previous per-batch spin and switched to a serialized dispatch path. It fixed a race but traces show larger host->kernel gaps and more frequent kernel-choice swaps inside the same request window.
maria: Can you paste the perfetto flame or a short timeline snippet? The queue_time vs compute time view is what we need.
sam: Perfetto link: https://perfetto.internal/trace/1743501122 and quick nsys CLI I ran:
```
nsys profile --sample=none --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=cpu_drift_1743501122 qrun -- ./run_infer --model=m --seq=4096 --batching=continuous --iters=400
```
simon: Quick read: compute time per token hasn't changed much, but queue_time variance increased a lot. KV cache hit rate down ~2% in this run (maybe ordering changed).
kai: Hmm — could the continuous-batch window heuristics be expanding because host-side timing moved? If windows grow we get more small micro-batches which triggers different kernel choices.
sam: I dumped batch-window sizes for the failing run: median microbatches per window went 8 -> 12, 95th pct went 16 -> 34. So more kernels with smaller work each. That explains higher launch overhead and occasional switch to a higher-latency kernel.
maria: Do we have kernel switch counts? That would make it obvious.
simon: Yes — kernels-per-request avg rose from 1.8 to 2.4. Also noticed prefetch path invoked more frequently because KV cache check now happens after the serialized dispatch.
kai: Two immediate levers: (1) move KV cache hit-check before serialization so prefetch isn't unnecessarily triggered, (2) add hysteresis to kernel chooser to avoid flipping on small batch-size deltas.
sam: Repro steps for local:
```
python -m bench.run --workload=eval --seq-len=4096 --iters=500 --batching=continuous --trace=perfetto --out=local_trace.pb
```
maria: I'll run with nsight on my workstation and capture L2/L3 and SM occupancy. If L3 thrash is up it would support the small-kernel overhead hypothesis.
simon: Also check kernel thresholds: we pick matmul-K1 for seq>128, fallback-K2 for smaller. With smaller microbatches overhead of K2 launch > K1 amortization. We should add a min-workload check before switching.
kai: I'll prototype hysteresis + min-workload filter and run the nightly canary. If it reduces p95 we can roll forward.
sam: Sounds good. I'll also try the quick experiment flipping serialized path back to old spin-once to verify it's the host timing causing the window expansion.
maria: Great — FYI I saw a small memory-copy increase in the nvtx slices around dispatch boundary; might be an extra memcpy we've introduced.
simon: If true, that could explain the extra host-side latency and KV miss cascade.
perf-bot: perf alert: p95 regression detected for job/nightly/4k-gen — linked traces added to thread.
kai: I'll open a PR with two toggles (hysteresis + prefetch-order) and link CI perf diff results. Assigning to @sam for validation. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks — I'll run the canary traces and post summaries here.
